`AlgebraicDynamics.jl` and `StockFlow.jl` currently resolve against an older
Catlab than `AlgebraicPetri.jl`, so this companion to the main vignette has
its own environment. It builds SIR as two composed resource sharers and as a
stock-and-flow diagram, and applies the same program as the main document to
both.

```{julia}
using CategoricalInterventions
using AlgebraicDynamics
using Catlab.Programs
using Catlab.WiringDiagrams: oapply
using ComponentArrays
using DiffEqCallbacks
using LabelledArrays
using OrdinaryDiffEq
using Plots
using StockFlow
using StockFlow.Syntax

default(; linewidth=2, grid=false)

infection_dynamics(u, p, t) = (rate = p.inf * u[1] * u[2]; [-rate, rate])
recovery_dynamics(u, p, t)  = (rate = p.rec * u[1]; [-rate, rate])

infection = ContinuousResourceSharer{Float64}(2, infection_dynamics)
recovery  = ContinuousResourceSharer{Float64}(2, recovery_dynamics)

sir_pattern = @relation (S, I, R) begin
    infection(S, I)
    recovery(I, R)
end
sir_system = oapply(sir_pattern, [infection, recovery])
```

The composed system keeps a positional state vector, so the model is told
the state names in order. Parameters are labelled with `ComponentArrays`.

```{julia}
model = Model(sir_system; states=[:S, :I, :R], parameters=[:inf, :rec],
              invariants=[Conserved([:S, :I, :R])])

program = @interventions model begin
    lockdown    = scale(:inf, 0.5; during=5.0..25.0)
    vaccination = transfer(:S => :R, 50.0; at=15.0)
end

u0 = [990.0, 10.0, 0.0]
p0 = ComponentArray(inf=0.05 * 10.0 / sum(u0), rec=0.25)
tspan = (0.0, 40.0)
grid = 0.0:0.5:40.0

sol = simulate(model, program; u0, p0, tspan, alg=Tsit5(), saveat=grid)
sol[3, end], sum(sol.u[end])
```

## StockFlow

A stock-and-flow diagram becomes a model whose parameters are its
parameters and whose states are its stocks. Labelled arrays supply the
names to the solver.

```{julia}
sf = @stock_and_flow begin
    :stocks
    S
    I
    R

    :parameters
    inf
    rec

    :dynamic_variables
    v_infection = inf * S * I
    v_recovery = rec * I

    :flows
    S => f_infection(v_infection) => I
    I => f_recovery(v_recovery) => R

    :sums
    N = [S, I, R]
end
stockflow = Model(sf; invariants=[Conserved([:S, :I, :R])])

u0l = LVector(S=990.0, I=10.0, R=0.0)
p0l = LVector(inf=p0.inf, rec=p0.rec)
sf_sol = simulate(stockflow, program; u0=u0l, p0=p0l, tspan, alg=Tsit5(), saveat=grid)
sf_sol[3, end], maximum(abs, Array(sol) .- Array(sf_sol))
```

## Cross-check against the direct equations

```{julia}
sir_ode(u, p, t) = [-p.inf * u[1] * u[2], p.inf * u[1] * u[2] - p.rec * u[2], p.rec * u[2]]
direct = Model(sir_ode; parameters=[:inf, :rec], states=Dict(:S => 1, :I => 2, :R => 3))
direct_sol = simulate(direct, program; u0, p0, tspan, alg=Tsit5(), saveat=grid)
maximum(abs, Array(sol) .- Array(direct_sol))
```

```{julia}
plot(sol.t, sol[3, :]; label="AlgebraicDynamics", xlabel="time", ylabel="R(t)",
     title="Same program: resource sharer, stock-and-flow, direct ODE")
plot!(sf_sol.t, sf_sol[3, :]; label="StockFlow", linestyle=:dash)
plot!(direct_sol.t, direct_sol[3, :]; label="direct ODE", linestyle=:dot)
```

## What the category theory bought

The same statement as in the main document: the program's meaning is fixed
by its algebra and schedule before a model is chosen (`apply_pullback`,
`lower_eq_apply`), so a composed resource sharer and a hand-written vector
field, and a stock-and-flow diagram, receive identical callbacks.
